text: What is migration in ornithology?
Which season commonly brings Arctic-breeding birds southward?
What is a stopover site?
choices: A place used only for nesting
A route segment over open water
A temporary refueling or resting area

text: Which resource most directly supports migratory flight?
What does a flyway describe?
The Atlantic Flyway primarily follows which region?
Which cue can provide directional information during clear nights?
Why do migrants often increase feeding before departure?
What is a migration wave?
Which observation best indicates nocturnal migration?
choices: Bird echoes detected overhead at night

text: What is the main purpose of a bird band or ring?
choices: Mark an individual for later identification

text: Which weather condition often assists broad-front migration?
What is a broad-front migration pattern?
choices: Movement spread across a wide landscape
Movement limited to a single flock

text: Which North American flyway follows the central plains and Mississippi basin?
What does photoperiod mean for migratory birds?
Which body tissue usually provides the principal fuel for long flights?
Why are wetlands valuable to many migrants?
What is a vagrant bird?
choices: A bird outside its expected range
A bird with no flight feathers

text: Which instrument is commonly used to study birds aloft at night?
What does site fidelity mean in migration studies?
choices: Repeated use of a particular site

text: Which behavior can reduce energy costs during flock flight?
What is a migratory divide?
choices: A region separating routes or directions

text: Which feature often guides migrants along a coast?
What is stopover duration?
choices: Time spent flying over a storm
Time between arrival and departure at a stopover
Time needed to grow a bill

text: Which migration route is associated with western North America?
How does a crosswind usually affect a migrant's ground track?
choices: It removes the need for orientation
It changes the bird into a glider

text: What is vector navigation?
Which cue is especially useful near coasts during daytime?
What does Zugunruhe refer to?
Why can tailwinds improve migration efficiency?
choices: They reduce required airspeed for progress
They remove the need for fuel

text: Which measurement best estimates a migrant's energetic condition?
What can a geolocator generally estimate?
choices: Approximate latitude and longitude from light data

text: What is an ecological trap at a stopover?
choices: A high-quality site with abundant food
A site that appears suitable but lowers survival
A net used for harmless capture

text: Which factor can make a stopover habitat especially productive?
What does compensatory orientation describe?
choices: Correcting displacement to maintain a destination

text: Which technique can reveal an individual bird's route repeatedly?
Why do many migrants avoid flying in heavy precipitation?
choices: It raises energetic and visibility costs

text: What is a refueling rate at a stopover?
choices: Rate of mass or energy gain

text: Which feather group is typically replaced during a complete molt?
How can molt constrain migration?
choices: It makes birds immune to wind
It competes for energy and can reduce flight performance
It eliminates the need for stopovers

text: What does a stable-isotope feather signature help infer?
Which radar pattern often indicates mass bird movement?
choices: A broad moving biological reflectivity pattern

text: What is a nocturnal migration call used for in monitoring?
choices: Detecting and sometimes identifying migrants overhead

text: Which mark-recapture result most directly estimates local stopover survival?
What is partial migration?
choices: Only some individuals of a population migrate
Migration during only half a day
Movement with one wing held still
A route crossing half a continent

text: What is an irruption?
Which resource often drives boreal finch irruptions?
What is a drift migrant?
choices: A bird carried off course by winds
A bird that refuses all wind assistance

text: Which method can test whether birds use star patterns?
In a classic orientation funnel, what does scratch direction represent?
What does clock-shift experimentation test?
Which manipulation can test magnetic orientation?
What is a magnetic inclination compass?
choices: A system sensitive to field angle as well as polarity
A compass based only on sunset color
A device that measures wing loading

text: Which sensory cue can provide a sunset compass?
Why are young migrants important in navigation research?
choices: Their first routes reveal inherited and learned components

text: What is route memory in an experienced migrant?
choices: A learned association with a recurring route
A permanent change in eye color
A feather pattern inherited after molt

text: Which physiological change commonly accompanies pre-migratory preparation?
What is flight muscle hypertrophy?
choices: Seasonal loss of red blood cells

text: Why can migrants digest food rapidly at stopovers?
choices: They can remodel digestive organs with demand
They rely only on stored water

text: Which hormone is strongly associated with seasonal migratory state?
What does aerodynamic wing loading influence?
How can wind affect a bird's airspeed choice?
choices: Birds may adjust heading and speed to optimize travel
Birds lose all control of heading

text: What is a thermal during migration?
choices: A rising column of warm air

text: Which migrants most often exploit thermals?
What is barrier crossing in flyway ecology?
choices: Traversing deserts, oceans, or mountain ranges
Changing from juvenile to adult plumage

text: Why can islands be critical stopovers?
choices: They provide scarce landfall and food across barriers

text: What is a migration bottleneck?
choices: A site where many migrants concentrate through limited geography

text: Which field count best samples passage at a coastal bottleneck?
choices: Standardized visual counts by time and effort

text: What does radar vertical profiling add to migration studies?
choices: Exact individual identity for every bird

text: Which radar signal feature can help separate birds from insects?
choices: Target size, speed, and texture patterns
Only the color of the sky

text: What is a Motus telemetry station used to detect?
Why are nanotags useful in migration studies?
choices: They provide detections over receiver networks
They identify age from plumage color

text: What is a geofence in tracking analysis?
choices: A virtual boundary that triggers a location event
A physical fence around a nest
A weather front crossing a flyway
A ring placed on a tarsus

text: Which limitation commonly affects light-level geolocators?
choices: Latitude and longitude estimates can be uncertain
They weigh more than the bird

text: What is calibration for a geolocator?
choices: Relating recorded light transitions to known locations

text: Why do researchers minimize tag mass?
choices: To reduce effects on behavior and energetics

text: What does a stable-isotope isoscape provide?
choices: A geographic pattern of isotope values
A map of radar reflectivity only

text: Which tissue is often sampled after migration for isotope analysis?
What is carry-over effect in annual migration?
choices: A prior season's condition influencing later performance
A bird carrying nesting material across oceans
A feather passing from one bird to another
A route copied by unrelated species

text: How can drought alter migration phenology?
choices: It can shift food timing and departure dates

text: What is phenological mismatch?
choices: Arrival and peak food availability become unsynchronized

text: Which approach best tests a stopover's habitat value?
choices: Compare fuel gain and survival with standardized effort
Count species once without effort data

text: What is a capture–recapture encounter history?
choices: A sequence of detections and nondetections for marked individuals
A list of every species in a region
A record of one bird's wingbeat
A map of unoccupied nest boxes

text: Which model estimates detection probability separately from survival?
What is a Barker model especially able to incorporate?
choices: Dead recoveries and live resightings between occasions

text: Why standardize mist-net effort across sites?
choices: To improve comparability of capture rates

text: Which measurement is most useful for estimating wing loading?
What does fuel deposition rate require repeated measurement of?
choices: Body mass over time with known effort

text: What is the migratory connectivity concept?
choices: Linking breeding and nonbreeding populations geographically
Linking molt feathers on one wing

text: Why does strong migratory connectivity matter for conservation?
choices: Threats at one location can affect a specific breeding population

text: Which analysis can infer population structure from tracking origins?
choices: Assignment of individuals to spatial source groups

text: What is leapfrog migration?
choices: Northern breeders winter farther south than southern breeders
Birds alternate left and right wings
A flock crosses a fence by jumping
A bird skips every other stopover

text: What is differential migration?
choices: Age, sex, or condition classes use different routes or timing
Every individual follows the same route
Only one species migrates each year

text: How can sexual size dimorphism affect migration timing?
choices: Different body sizes can alter fuel economics and departure schedules
It prevents either sex from crossing barriers

text: What is protandry in avian migration?
choices: Males arrive or depart earlier than females

text: Which evidence most strongly supports innate compass calibration?
choices: Young birds orient directionally without prior route experience
Tagged birds use a known stopover

text: What is the main inferential risk of treating radar echoes as species counts?
choices: Different taxa can produce overlapping signatures

text: Which design best separates weather effects from seasonal timing?
choices: Replicate observations across years and weather conditions
Observe one storm at one site
Use only dates without weather data

text: What is a null model in migration orientation analysis?
choices: A specified expectation of random or baseline headings
A bird with no migration route

text: Why use circular statistics for orientation data?
choices: Headings wrap around at north and require angular methods

text: What does the Rayleigh test commonly assess?
choices: Whether angular observations depart from uniformity
Whether two masses have equal variance

text: What is an axial orientation distribution?
choices: A pattern where opposite directions are treated as equivalent
A distribution of wing axes by length
A count of birds on one axis

text: Which control is important in a cue-manipulation experiment?
choices: A comparable group experiencing unchanged cues
A different species in another continent
A site selected after seeing results

text: What is pseudoreplication in migration research?
choices: Treating nonindependent observations as independent replicates
Using two tags on one bird

text: Why can light pollution alter nocturnal migration?
choices: It can disrupt orientation and attract or disorient birds
It prevents birds from hearing calls

text: What is a mortality sink along a flyway?
choices: A location where losses exceed replacement or safe passage
A site with unusually rapid fueling
A radar station with no birds

text: Which field protocol best detects collision mortality at a lit building?
choices: Repeated standardized carcass searches with removal and detection trials
One search after an unrelated storm

text: What does a double-observer survey help estimate?
choices: Detection probability for birds seen by observers

text: Why record observer effort in migration counts?
choices: Counts need effort to compare rates among periods or sites

text: What is an encounter probability in ringing studies?
choices: The chance a marked bird is detected during a sampling occasion
The chance a bird chooses a nest cavity

text: Which conclusion is strongest when multiple tracking methods agree?
choices: Route inference is more robust to method-specific bias
Every individual uses the same path
